notes: Read SKILL.md and references/job-testing.md, background-jobs-chaining.md, job-patterns.md, job-monitoring.md, queue-setup.md, background-jobs-fundamentals.md, job-types.md, job-scheduling.md, background-jobs-advanced.md in full. Designs background job systems: queue backend selection, queue topology with DLQs, job contracts with idempotency keys, retry with backoff and jitter, worker concurrency, graceful shutdown, cron scheduling, sagas, and monitoring (BullMQ, Celery, asynq, Hangfire, SQS).

No commands, installs, credentials, or network access by the agent; the output is design text and sample code. Sample code reads Redis connection settings from environment variables and the guidance says never to put secrets in job payloads (SKILL.md:563, 631).

Code-quality caveats a user should know: the Bull Board snippets (SKILL.md:502, job-types.md:188) mount /admin/queues with no auth middleware, although SKILL.md:569 says the admin UI requires authentication; the lock release at queue-setup.md:172-174 deletes without an owner check and job-scheduling.md:146-162 has an odd cron check and uses Redis KEYS; SKILL.md:367 and queue-setup.md:7 use BullMQ QueueScheduler, which is deprecated in BullMQ 2+; the idempotency check at SKILL.md:345-358 is check-then-act (job-patterns.md:174-199 shows the locked version). SKILL.md:646 hands off to an optional `backend-event-driven` skill that is not bundled.
